title: Edge resize rail and density visualization for virtual table
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The table component is the primary surface used across Console and runtime dashboards. Teams repeatedly ask for a way to resize very narrow columns without accidental drags and to understand density state at a glance. Problem: On virtualized tables with continuous scrolling, small column handles are hard to target and resizing typically collapses content unexpectedly. Additionally, current density toggles are global and lack per-table visual feedback. Goal: Introduce an edge-oriented resize rail (a wider, forgiving hit target attached to column edges) that supports both pointer and keyboard resizing, plus an inline density visualization meter in the table header that communicates current density and per-column compression levels. Key constraints: must not regress virtualization performance, must work with keyboard-only flows and screen readers, should be compatible with sticky headers and grouped columns, and should be implementable without large runtime changes. Proposed approach: 1) Edge resize rail: render a 12px invisible hit-rail at column boundaries (visualized on hover/focus) which initiates resize. When visible, show a subtle rail with drag affordance, snap points, and a drag preview overlay. 2) Proximity-aware activation: rail becomes active only when pointer is within a 20px proximity or when column is focused via keyboard. 3) Compression indicator: small density meter (3-segment bar) in right side of header cell showing current compression ratio (expanded/normal/compressed). Clicking the metric cycles presets (Expanded, Default, Compact) for that column group. 4) Accessibility: rails reachable via roving-tabindex; keyboard resize using Arrow keys with Shift/Alt modifiers for coarse/fine steps; aria-live updates for resize value and density changes. 5) Metrics & telemetry: add telemetry hooks for frequency of rail usage, average resize delta, and density preset toggles to inform defaults. Acceptance criteria: - Edge rail appears on hover/focus and provides a 12px hit area without affecting layout. - Keyboard-only users can focus a column boundary and resize in 1px increments; screen readers announce "Column width set to X pixels". - Density meter reflects effective column compression and toggles presets per-column-group. - No measurable degradation (>2%) in scroll/paint metrics for 10k row virtualized table regression tests. - Design tokens provided for rail color, hover, active, and meter states. Deliverables: Figma frames (interaction + token spec), accessibility spec doc, final annotated component design, implementation notes for runtime team, sample storybook entry, and test plan for perf and a11y. Links: Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/table-edge-rail-proto Confluence PRD: https://confluence.internal/re/bigtable-edge-rail Prototype (video): https://drive.internal/re/edge-rail-demo GitHub PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/REDACTED
